title: check-trailers names a body line starting with a lowercase skill name such as kb-sprint: as a stray trailer and refuses the push
goal: check-trailers, the commit-msg hook and sync's gate no longer name a body line that starts with a lowercase skill or tool name followed by a colon (kb-sprint:, kb-backlog:, kb-worker:) as a stray trailer, while a stray KB-Work, KB-* or Self-Reviewed line above the trailer block is still named and refused. Found by the SP-gkbtjjce review: kg_trailers.STRAY_KEY is compiled with re.I since BG-dsab2ti3, and 51bd8c38 on main (body opening 'kb-sprint: the planning commit before the claim sync') would be refused if pushed today.

gates.question: How should kg_trailers.STRAY_KEY tell a stray trailer from a prose line like 'kb-sprint: ...'?

notes: Premise (2026-10-08, plan of SP-vayhvwfy): the repro names 'not a trailer: kb-sprint: the planning commit before the claim sync.' as BAD, exit 1: reproduces. Gate stray-key options: known-keys = STRAY_KEY matches, case-insensitively, only the trailer keys kg_trailers knows (KB-Work, KB-Auto, the other KB-* keys it writes or reads, Self-Reviewed), so a lowercase 'kb-work:' typo is still refused and 'kb-sprint:' passes (recommended: keeps BG-dsab2ti3's typo catch); case-sensitive = drop re.I, so only 'KB-' and 'Self-Reviewed' in their own case count, and a lowercase typo of a real key passes unread. Check 1 passes before the work and why: it pins that a stray KB-Work line above the trailer block is still named and refused (the goal's second clause); the repro proves the fix.
